$what: Provenance of aurora-effects-scene.schema.json — empyrean's CONTRACT schema, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. scene.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/effects-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Until 2026-08-29 the pinned blob hash lived as a `const PINNED_BLOB` in effects-schema-drift.test.ts and as prose in scene.ts's header and in effects-scene-golden.test.ts's header. Three copies, one of which (scene.ts) had already gone THREE re-pins stale without anything going red, because nothing hashes a comment. The hash now lives HERE, once, and the test reads it. The prose citations remain prose and say so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path-probe design would degrade to 'schema not found -> skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check below are the payment. See docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md for the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable — this file is never read from ../empyrean at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision.
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. It is also deliberately outside test/fixtures/ because the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks that tree and reads every 40-hex on a `revision*` key as an AEON revision; an empyrean SHA sitting there would be checked for reachability from aeon's master and fail for a reason that has nothing to do with it.

what_changed_at_this_pin.semantic: EXACTLY ONE addition, and it is a ROOT key, not a layer one: `properties/reels`, inserted between `v_deform` and `anchor` — EFFECTS-W1 DoD item 10's authoring half, empyrean AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md §2.7, filed against aeon's decision note docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-reels-per-scene-key-shape.md at aeon 660aabc0. One required member, `rates`: an array of EXACTLY FIVE integers (`minItems`/`maxItems` 5), each -128..127, `uniqueItems: true`, in SCREEN ORDER (index i owns screen X 64i..64i+63). `unevaluatedProperties: false`, so the root's own closure plus this node's makes a `cols_per_band` key a refusal rather than an extension point. The root object stays CLOSED and now has EIGHTEEN properties (schema, id, name, layers, v_factor, v_center, v_offset, v_factor_fg, bob_shift, bob_period, deform_fg, deform_bg, v_deform, reels, anchor, left_column_mask, transition, budget_class), counted from the vendored bytes rather than from the CR's prose. what_changed_at_this_pin.how_the_one_was_separated: TWO INDEPENDENT READINGS, run in Aurora by `scratchpad/schema-revendor-proof.mjs --old <HEAD bytes> --new <vendored>`; it exits 1 ("structure moved") and both readings AGREE. Reading 2, every `description` stripped at every depth and keys re-sorted: 5904 -> 6122 characters, not byte-identical — the correct verdict for a structural addition, and the check a description-only reading alone could not make. Neither document was retyped; both were extracted through git objects. ⚠ THE TWELVE AGREE WITH empyrean's OWN COUNT this time (its commit message says "0 changed, 0 removed, 12 added"), and unlike the rowRemap pin below there is no empty-container node for a pointer-to-scalar walk to miss — `reels` declares no `"not": {}` and no other valueless container — so the leaf diff is not blind here. Counted rather than relayed all the same.
what_changed_at_this_pin.the_hazard_this_pin_carries: ONE UNIT THAT LOOKS LIKE ANOTHER FIELD'S, AND A TIER NO KEYWORD CAN EXPRESS. (1) `rates` IS SIGNED WHOLE PIXELS PER FRAME. There is NO FIXED POINT anywhere on this path — the engine does `add.b (a2)+, d0` into a byte phase that wraps mod 256. `drift.rate`'s ×256 export conversion MUST NOT be applied here: a panel or converter copied from the drift path emits 768 for an intended 3, and this -128..127 bound is the ONLY place that mistake is caught today (the engine has no magnitude ensure yet; aeon's implementing parcel adds one). The bound catches it for every intended rate except 0 — which is asserted, derived from the schema's own two numbers, in test/formats/effects-reels.test.ts. Aurora routes `reels` through NO shared rate converter: the ×256 lives only in `driftPxPerFrameToRate` / `driftRateToPxPerFrame` (scene-ui.ts), both named for drift, and nothing in the reels path calls them. (2) ZERO IS ALLOWED, deliberately unlike `drift.rate`, whose schema spells `"not": {"const": 0}`. A stationary strip among moving ones is a real authored choice; `uniqueItems` caps it at one occurrence. Two adjacent keys, opposite rulings on the same literal. (3) SCREEN ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER. Index i owns screen X 64i..64i+63. The contract says an editor that sorts `rates` or round-trips them through a dict keyed by band name "silently relocates every strip"; the generator emits in document order, verbatim. Aurora's codec does not normalise arrays through any keyed structure — `canonicalizeBySchema` maps arrays positionally and `canonicalJsonPretty` sorts OBJECT keys only — and a permutation round-trip is asserted rather than argued. (4) DEBUG TIER, AND NO JSON KEYWORD CAN SAY SO. The mechanism's table, proc and on-switch all sit inside `if DEBUG == 1` (OJZ_Reel_Speed's emitted length is 0 in release, aeon ojz_effects.emp:1766-1767), so a scene saved with `reels` shows NOTHING in a release build. A future panel MUST say that on screen. It is NOT capability-gated: no CAP_ bit for reels exists, and a generator arm must not emit a check that does not exist — so Aurora adds none. (5) SCHEMA-LEGAL IS NOT ALWAYS BUILDABLE. aeon's generator REFUSES `reels` on a scene whose sections resolve through a preset (Effects_ResolveParallax rung 2) or the act default (rung 3), because the association table is keyed on the lowered config label and that label is unique only at rung 1 (an editor `sceneRef`). That refusal is aeon's to make; anything Aurora says about it is ADVISORY and must say so in its own words.
what_changed_at_this_pin.aurora_edits_this_pin_forced: (1) `uniqueItems` IN json-schema-subset.ts — THE COVERAGE GATE NAMED IT, both halves: the keyword census ("every keyword in the committed schema is implemented") and the whole-schema walk (`assertSchemaSupported`) went red together. It is the FIRST `uniqueItems` in either committed contract schema. Implemented as a real assertion with an order-insensitive structural equality of its own (`sameInstance`), NOT the file's existing `deepEqual`, whose `JSON.stringify` comparison calls two objects with the same members in different key order DISTINCT — which would silently ACCEPT a duplicate the real schema rejects, this evaluator's one forbidden failure mode. `uniqueItems: false` is accepted as the no-op it is defined to be; any non-boolean value is refused by shape at assertSupported. Added to NON_ANNOTATING_KEYWORDS too: it is a pure instance assertion and names no property as evaluated, so it cannot weaken the `unevaluatedProperties`-as-`additionalProperties` equivalence. (2) THE SHAPE-COVERAGE GOLDEN test/fixtures/effects/canopy_dusk.json HAD TO GAIN THE KEY, because effects-scene-golden.test.ts derives 'every declared TOP-LEVEL key is exercised' from the schema and went red naming `reels` — the gate working as designed. It carries aeon's own shipped rates, [3, -5, 2, -4, 6] (OJZ_REEL_SPEEDS, games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:1756 at aeon 660aabc0), so the fixture is the corpus rather than five numbers this repo invented. Re-emitted by the OTHER implementation §5 names (`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` plus the §8 terminator), never by serializeEffectsScene, so the byte round-trip stays cross-implementation evidence. (3) EffectsScene gained `reels?: EffectsReels` in scene.ts, plus `EFFECTS_REEL_BAND_COUNT` and `EFFECTS_REEL_RATE_BOUNDS` read out of the schema node. The codec needed no other change: parse hands back what JSON.parse produced and serialize is schema-driven, so an absent key stays absent and a present one round-trips in document order.
